arcs.title: Dana: Haifa
arcs.stage: Mon: he asked her out for Saturday after Shabbat (a walk, falafel at Avi's); she said yes, 'things change in January'. Tue: trivia night at Cafe Nahat, Dana is the quizmaster, Ishai plays with Noa and Tomer. Next: first date Sat Nov 21; she almost tells him.
arcs.secret: Dana has been offered a job running a new cafe in Haifa from January and must answer by Mon Dec 7. She has not told Ishai.

arcs.title: Gadi: Unpaid
arcs.stage: Mon: Hanukkah files to Gadi only; Ruti asked for Ishai's number ('we're a team'); a free dreidel 'when the invoice has a number'; Gadi promised a number by Thursday. Tue: quiet. Next: the Thursday number, then Ruti calls Ishai directly (week 2).
arcs.secret: Sababa Creative lost its biggest client in October. Gadi is paying every freelancer late and hides it behind cheerful 'small things'.

arcs.title: Noa: Shir
arcs.stage: Mon night: the duffel and the taped box 'S.' by the closet ('winter stuff, don't open'), Shir's name face down; he circled the box all evening and didn't open it. Tue: a 07:02 text about three plumbers 'from the British Mandate' (Sivan doesn't buy it); after trivia she sleeps at his place, an 'Eilat hotel client' at ten, a cracked late call on the stairs ('not on the phone, not tonight'). Wed: second couch night. Next: Sat Nov 28 he finds out.
arcs.secret: Noa's girlfriend of three years, Shir, moved out in October. Noa told nobody: it's why she is late, cancels plans and pushes Ishai's love life so hard.

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: The notebook: 'I want to talk to Dana', 'I want a date (payment kind)', 'I want: one invoice'. Tue at the gym he tells Sivan he has a list ('number one is a person, number two is an invoice'). Lesson 3 Thu Nov 19.

arcs.title: Mrs. Levi's cough
arcs.stage: Mon: hoarse, gave Ishai the cats' bowl (the grey one is Ben-Gurion); no doctor. Tue: Ishai helps her record a voice message to Eli ('everything is fine, I'm very busy too'), she coughs through it and deletes it; 'tomorrow I'll see' about a doctor. Next (week 2): bronchitis, Ishai feeds the cats daily.
arcs.secret: Mrs. Levi is lonely: her son Eli in Toronto hasn't visited in four years, and she always says he's busy.

arcs.title: Avi's kiosk
arcs.stage: Thu: 'Double? From January?' overheard. Tue: no proverb ('today the tahini is the proverb'), an envelope with a lawyer's stamp in his apron, a call he lets ring; 'monuments don't pay rent'. Ishai offered a free design; Avi refused. Next (week 2): no proverbs at all.
arcs.secret: Avi's landlord is doubling the kiosk's rent from January.

arcs.title: Lior's novel and Moshe
arcs.stage: Sun: chapter eleven, 'the man finally answers a question'. Mon: chapter twelve, 'she says yes, I didn't plan that'; tells Ishai there aren't many weeks. Ishai still doesn't recognise himself.
arcs.secret: Lior's novel is about Ishai: 'the man who apologises to his coffee'.

arcs.title: Tomer and Noa
arcs.stage: Mon: leftover lamb soup with Ishai; Noa's 'good maybe' for Wednesday. Tue: trivia with Noa and Ishai (HERZL HEADS); he argues every answer with Dana, showing off. Wed Nov 18: the Pump House gallery night (Quiet Signals).
arcs.secret: Tomer has liked Noa since school.

arcs.title: Mr. Zelig's bench
arcs.stage: Sat: one true sentence for the photo; Dana sat on his bench Thursday 'looking at her phone like it was the sea... not this sea'. 1971: 'I stayed.'

beats.goal: Morning treadmill at Herzl Gym next to Sivan (competitive, deadpan). Ishai tells her he has a list of wants now ('number one is a person, number two is an invoice'). Noa texts that three plumbers have been at hers since seven, 'pipes from the British Mandate'; Sivan says nobody in Tel Aviv gets a plumber at seven. Ishai shrugs it off. Sivan sets his speed to six and books him for Wednesday.
beats.teaser: Sivan reads Noa's morning text over Ishai's shoulder, and frowns
beats.forceText: On the treadmill next to Sivan, Ishai reads Noa's text about three plumbers at seven; Sivan doesn't believe it.

forceLines.say: Three plumbers at seven? In Tel Aviv? Nobody gets one before ten.
She said chaos. With two exclamation marks.

forceCommentary.say: Sivan's not buying the plumbers. Neither am I.
'Pipes from the British Mandate.' Too much detail. Classic tell.

moments.text: Herzl Gym at eight. Ishai steps onto the treadmill next to Sivan, who is already running at a pace he can't read. Channel 9 morning news on the left screen.

lines.say: Husky guy. You came back. I had money on never.
He's not a husky. He's a... mostly a dog.
Ten minutes again? Or a whole warm-up today?
Twenty. I wrote it down. I'm a man with a list now.
A list. What's on it?
Things I want. Out loud. It's homework from a class.
Number one, I hope, is 'run faster than a bus'.
Number one is a person. Number two is an invoice.
Invoice beats person. Invoices don't cancel on you.
You'd like my friend Noa. She says things like that.

commentary.say: A list of wants and number one is a person. Somebody text the cafe.
Sivan runs like her rent is due. Respect.

moments.text: His phone buzzes on the treadmill's ledge. He reads the text while still walking, slows down and nearly steps off the belt.

message.say: Plumbers here since seven!! Three of them. Total chaos, pipes from the British Mandate. Trivia tonight, then your couch. Love you, bye

lines.say: Pipes from the British Mandate. She sent that at two past seven.
You're reading on a treadmill. That's how people die.
My friend has plumbers. Three. Since seven.
Three plumbers at seven? In Tel Aviv? Nobody gets one before ten.
She said chaos. With two exclamation marks.
Two is a lot for chaos. Chaos only needs one.
She's sleeping at my place tonight. And tomorrow.
Then buy a second pillow. And speed up, you're at four.
Four is a speed. Four is honest.

commentary.say: Three plumbers before breakfast in this city? Sivan smells it. So do I.
'Pipes from the British Mandate.' Nobody lies with that much history unless they're lying.

moments.text: Sivan hops off, towel round her neck, and taps his speed up to six on her way past. He keeps up for almost a minute, then steps off, red-faced, to talk.

lines.say: Six. Don't touch it. I'll know.
How will you know? You're leaving.
Michal tells me everything. She's by the mirror.
She invited me to her Friday run club. She doesn't go.
Nobody goes. It's a club for feeling guilty on Fridays.
Then I'm already a member.
Ha. Okay, husky guy. Same time Thursday?
Thursday is the class. Wednesday?
Wednesday. Twenty-five minutes. Put it on your list.
Under the invoice. Above the person. No. Below.

commentary.say: He held six for almost a minute. Alert the Olympic committee.
'Below the person.' He corrected himself. I rest my case.

update.memory: The husky guy came back for twenty minutes and held six for almost a minute. Has a list of wants. His friend's 7 AM plumbers sound fake.

beats.goal: Lunch at Avi's falafel kiosk after the lecture. Avi works in silence and gives no proverb for the first time ('today the tahini is the proverb'); an envelope with a lawyer's stamp sticks out of his apron and he lets a call ring out. Ishai asks if everything is okay; Avi blames chickpeas and oil, says 'monuments don't pay rent'. Ishai offers a free design; Avi refuses ('free you give to your mother'). Ishai does not learn about the rent.
beats.teaser: Avi hands Ishai a falafel, and for once, no proverb
beats.forceText: At Avi's kiosk there is no proverb today; an envelope with a lawyer's stamp sticks out of Avi's apron and he blames the price of chickpeas.

forceLines.say: And the proverb? You always give one with the tahini.
Today the tahini is the proverb.

forceCommentary.say: Avi without a proverb is a sky without a sun. Something's wrong.
That envelope has a lawyer's stamp. Nobody gets good news on letterhead.

moments.text: The lunch queue at Avi's kiosk is short. Avi fries in silence; a folded envelope with a lawyer's stamp sticks out of his apron pocket. Ishai waits for the proverb that always comes with the pita.

lines.say: Ishai. Half or whole?
Whole. And the proverb? You always give one with the tahini.
Today the tahini is the proverb.
That's not a proverb. That's tahini.
Exactly. Simple. Pickles?
Yes, please. Avi, is everything okay? You're quiet.
Quiet is cheaper. Everything is getting expensive, even talking.
Chickpeas again?
Chickpeas. Oil. Everything. Eat, it's hot.
Thank you. Full price. Don't argue.

commentary.say: No proverb. Avi without a proverb is a sky without a sun.
That envelope has a lawyer's stamp. Nobody gets good news on letterhead.

moments.text: Ishai eats leaning on the counter. Avi's phone rings; he looks at the name, lets it ring out and pushes the envelope deeper into his apron.

lines.say: You can answer. I'll watch the buses.
It's nobody. Somebody who thinks he's somebody.
Thirty years you're here, right? Since before the bank.
Thirty-one in March. I remember when the bank was a shoe shop.
Then nobody can move you. You're a monument.
Monuments don't pay rent, Ishai. Pigeons sit on them.
Is that a proverb?
No. That's just true. There's a difference.
If you need anything. A sign, a new menu. I'll design it free.
Free you give to your mother. Eat your falafel.

commentary.say: 'Thirty-one in March.' He's counting. People who count are worried.
Ishai offered free design work. Somewhere, Gadi just felt a disturbance.

update.memory: Ishai noticed I had no proverb today and offered a free design. I said nothing about the letter. He paid full price again.

beats.goal: Mrs. Levi sits on a kitchen chair on the landing, coughing, and asks Ishai to help her send a voice message to her son Eli in Toronto. She records 'Eli, motek, it's Ima, everything is fine, I'm very busy too', coughs through it and deletes it so he won't worry. Ishai gently says Eli might want to worry a little and asks her to call a doctor; 'tomorrow I'll see'. Ben-Gurion the grey cat watches from the stairs.
beats.teaser: Mrs. Levi records a message for Eli, and deletes it
beats.forceText: On the landing Ishai helps Mrs. Levi record a voice message to Eli; she coughs through it and deletes it.

forceLines.say: With coughing he'll worry. Then he'll call. Then he's late for work.
Maybe he'd want to worry. A little.

forceCommentary.say: 'I'm very busy too.' Nobody busy sits on a chair on the landing.
Ben-Gurion the cat has better boundaries than anyone in this building.

moments.text: Mrs. Levi sits on her kitchen chair on the landing in her cardigan, coughing, her phone held at arm's length. She waves Ishai over as he comes up the stairs.

lines.say: Ishai. Come. This telephone has a button that hates me.
Which one? Hi. You sound worse than yesterday.
It's the landing. Drafty. The microphone one. For a voice message.
Hold it down while you talk. Let go when you're done.
Hold, talk, let go. Like marriage.
Who's it for?
Eli. Today is nothing special. I just want to say hello.
Okay. Hold here. Go.
Eli, motek, it's Ima. Everything is fine. I'm very busy too...
Keep holding. It's still recording.

commentary.say: 'I'm very busy too.' Oh, Mrs. Levi. Nobody busy sits on a chair on the landing.
Hold, talk, let go. She's not wrong about marriage.

moments.text: A long coughing fit swallows the message. She lets go of the button, looks at the screen and deletes it before Ishai can stop her. Ben-Gurion the grey cat watches from the stairs.

lines.say: Why delete it? It was nice.
With coughing he'll worry. Then he'll call. Then he's late for work.
Maybe he'd want to worry. A little.
Sons don't want. Sons are busy. Toronto is a busy city.
Let me make you tea. The ginger one.
You made three on Friday. Two are still in my fridge.
Then I'll warm one. And tomorrow you call a doctor?
Tomorrow I'll see. Feed Ben-Gurion, he's looking at you.
He looks at everyone like that.
Only at people who feed him. Go, go. Thank you, motek.

commentary.say: Ben-Gurion has better boundaries than anyone in this building.
She deleted it. And 'tomorrow I'll see' is Hebrew for no.

update.memory: Ishai helped me with a voice message to Eli. I coughed and deleted it. He wants me to see a doctor. Tomorrow I'll see.

beats.goal: After trivia night Noa comes to sleep at Ishai's 'because of the plumbers'. Too cheerful; teases that Tomer showed off all night. Ishai asks about the plumbers and she piles on details ('very religious plumbers, early risers'). Her phone buzzes face down at ten; 'a hotel client in Eilat'. At half past ten Ishai brings a blanket to the corridor and finds her on the top stair ending a call: 'not on the phone, I can't, not tonight'. She says everything is amazing. He doesn't push. Ishai does NOT learn about Shir.
beats.teaser: Noa sleeps over 'for the plumbers', then a call on the stairs
beats.forceText: Noa sleeps at Ishai's after trivia; late at night he finds her on the stairs ending a call she won't explain.

forceLines.say: Two minutes. I like the stairs. Stairs don't ask anything.
Okay. Two minutes. The door's open.

forceCommentary.say: 'Stairs don't ask anything.' Saddest sentence of the week.
An emotional hotel in Eilat. At half past ten. On the stairs.

moments.text: After trivia, Noa comes in with a pillow under her arm and a toothbrush in her coat pocket, still buzzing from the quiz. She drops the pillow on the armchair like she owns it.

lines.say: Tomer argued every single answer with Dana. Every one. Showing off.
Showing off for who? Dana's busy. Saturday, with me.
For the room. Tomer shows off for furniture. He's sweet.
So how were the plumbers? Three, you said.
A nightmare. The pipes are from the Mandate. Lead. They poisoned the British.
Sivan at the gym says nobody gets a plumber at seven.
Who's Sivan? Is Sivan a plumber? No? Then Sivan doesn't know.
She runs at ten an hour. She knows things.
Mine came at seven. Very religious plumbers. Early risers. Can we have tea?
Tea. Yes. Sit.

commentary.say: 'Very religious plumbers.' She's building the lie live, with extensions.
Tomer shows off for furniture. Tomer shows off for one piece of furniture.

moments.text: Tea at the island. Noa's phone buzzes face down on the counter and keeps buzzing; she doesn't turn it over. Her eyes go to the taped box by the closet, then away.

lines.say: It's buzzing. Answer, I'll wash the cups.
It's a client. Clients at ten at night should be illegal.
Which client?
A hotel in Eilat. They want the logo to feel like 'a hug in August'.
That's actually a good brief.
Don't side with them. You side with me. Always.
Always. I didn't open the box, by the way.
I know. You'd have the face. The guilty face.
I don't have a guilty face.
You have only guilty face. It's why I love you. Go to bed.

commentary.say: A hotel in Eilat calling at ten. That hug in August is very persistent.
'You side with me. Always.' She needs that more than she's saying.

moments.text: Half past ten. Ishai brings a blanket out to the landing, where Noa sits on the top stair with her phone at her ear. She ends the call too fast when she sees him.

lines.say: ...not on the phone. I can't. Not tonight. Bye.
Sorry. Blanket. It's cold on the stairs.
Thanks. The hotel. Very emotional people in Eilat.
Noa. Is everything okay?
Everything's amazing. I'm at yours, there's tea, you have a date.
That's three things about me.
Because you're the interesting one this month. Enjoy it.
Come inside. Mrs. Levi will hear us.
Two minutes. I like the stairs. Stairs don't ask anything.
Okay. Two minutes. The door's open.

commentary.say: 'Stairs don't ask anything.' Noa, honey, saddest sentence of the week.
Three things about him. Zero about her. He noticed. Finally.

update.memory: Sleeping at Ishai's for the plumbers. He brought me a blanket on the stairs and asked if I'm okay. Said everything's amazing. He hasn't opened the box.

hook.text: Noa cut a late call on the stairs: 'not on the phone, not tonight'. Who is she really talking to, and what's in the box?

previously.text: Noa left the taped 'S.' box by the closet and told him not to open it. He circled it all evening, didn't touch it, and went to bed with it still taped.

hosts: Tuesday: lecture at eleven, trivia at half past seven. Busy man, for a man with no boss.
Today's lecture is about hoaxes. Fitting. Somebody in this show is running one.
Princess Caraboo fooled a whole English town for ten weeks. Some people manage it with plumbers.
Trivia night at Cafe Nahat. Dana with a microphone. Zohar, breathe.
HERZL HEADS against THE OWLS. My money's on the owls. They're up at night anyway.
Noa's sleeping at Ishai's tonight. 'For the plumbers.' I'll say no more. I'll say a little more later.
Moshe the basil had a quiet night. Oren checked. Twice.
I did not check twice. I checked once and then I confirmed.
That box marked 'S.' is still by the closet. Untouched. The man has the willpower of a monk.
Or he's scared of tape. Fifty-fifty.
Avi's kiosk, the queue at half past six. Best falafel on Herzl, ask anyone.
Mrs. Levi's game show is at seven thirty. She shouts the answers through the wall.
Saturday is the date. A walk and falafel. Four days. I'm counting, he's counting, Falafel the dog is counting.
Nobody tells Ishai anything this week. Have you noticed? Everybody's smiling and nobody's talking.
Gadi promised a number by Thursday. A number of what, he didn't say.
The Pump House tomorrow: Quiet Signals. Art you look at in silence. Tomer will talk through all of it.
Sivan at the gym runs faster than my Wi-Fi.
If Ishai apologises to a treadmill today, I win a bet.
Lior's novel is on chapter twelve. I'd read it. I feel like I already have.
Partly cloudy, twenty-one. Perfect weather for not saying what you mean.
School's out at half past one. Herzl Street gets loud, Ishai gets louder at his desk.
Piano practice upstairs at four. Same scale, every Tuesday. It's getting better. Slowly.
Somebody give Ishai a raise. Oh wait. That's the whole problem.
Dana asks the questions tonight. For once, Ishai has to answer out loud.
Ben-Gurion the cat is the most powerful resident of the building. Fight me.
radio: Radio Herzl 88.2, Tuesday morning. Partly cloudy, twenty-one. Sleeves optional.
If your plumber shows up before eight, call us. We'd like to interview him.
Traffic on Herzl is moving, the 88 is on time, which is news in itself.
Next up, a song for everyone pretending they're fine. Which is everyone.
Quiz night tonight somewhere in this city? Here's a free answer: it's never Sydney.
Our listener Rivka says her cat ignores her. Rivka, that's how they say I love you.
Tuesday fact: the average Tel Avivian says 'sababa' forty times a day. We counted. Badly.
Coming up after the news: forty minutes of songs about trains. Don't ask.
To the man who sings along on Herzl Street every morning: we hear you. Literally.
Weather tonight: mild. Perfect for sitting on the stairs and not talking.
Radio Herzl, eighty-eight point two. The only station that admits it's Tuesday.
A song for the night shift, the bakers and everyone up with a full head.

zelig: The pigeons are early today. Somebody is waiting for something.
A box that says one letter. One letter is a whole name, if you know.
In 1971 nobody had plumbers. We had brothers.
Tuesday. Even the duck looks busy.
michal: Run club Friday. I'll definitely come this time. Probably.
Sivan says the husky guy came back. Interesting.
Mirror, mirror, why do I look tired at nine.
lior: Chapter thirteen: the friend sleeps over. No. Too close. Keep it.
She said 'by December'. December is soon.
The man ordered his coffee without saying sorry. I have to rewrite page four.
Quiz night. Good. Everybody in one room, nobody saying the true thing.
kobi: Tuesday. Tuesday numbers are seven and thirty-one. Always.
One beer. Then the system. Then maybe one beer.
Quiz at the cafe? Quiz is lottery for people with glasses.
...no, listen, the lottery remembers you. It REMEMBERS.

street: ...and he said the rent's going up again, I said everything's going up...
...three plumbers? before eight? where does she live, Switzerland...
...Avi didn't even say anything clever today, I got worried...
...the 88 came on time, I almost missed it out of shock...
market: ...two kilo tomatoes and don't give me the soft ones...
...my son in Toronto, he calls Fridays, sometimes...
...this mint is from this morning, smell it, smell...
park: ...she says she's fine, everyone says they're fine...
...the duck has a name, I'm not telling you...
...ten minutes and back, the dog decides...
cafe: ...is it trivia tonight? I'm terrible at it, I'm coming...
...Haifa? no, I said I'd think about it...
...the guy in the corner writes the same page every day...

chat.say: Reminder: gas delivery at 10:00. Please leave the meter cupboard open.
Gas man at ten. Does he need keys, or do we just pray?
Who has lemons? Not for me. For a friend. Thank you.
Kids out of school, stair light still flickering. Moti, the receipt for the bulb?
The bulb is ordered. Patience is also a bulb.
Avi's queue goes to the corner today. Worth it.
Game show at 7:30. If you hear shouting, it's the correct answer.
Whoever is on the stairs, the light switch is on the left. Good night.
